source.note: supportWindows transcribed from docs/operator-manual/tested-kubernetes-versions.md. That file is a PLACEHOLDER on master — it is populated only on release branches, each listing its own version plus the two prior — so the matrix was assembled from release-3.5/3.2/2.14/2.11/2.8 and the overlapping rows cross-checked for contradictions (none). Each cell is a contiguous descending k8s list, which is what makes a min/max window a faithful representation rather than a widening; the generator asserts contiguity and refuses to transcribe a gapped cell. Floor is 2.6: release-2.5 and older ship no such table, so an older install reports VERSION_NOT_IN_CATALOG (honest 'no vendor data') rather than a guessed window. 2026-08-29: rules read from RELEASE branches, not master — origin/release-3.3 carries a breaking-change section (client-side-apply CRD size) that master's copy lost, and master's 3.3-3.4/3.4-3.5/3.5-3.6 guides contain empty placeholder sections where 'no entry' means 'not yet written', never 'no change'.

upgradeNotes.title: Logs RBAC is enforced by default — the pod Logs tab disappears without an explicit grant
upgradeNotes.quote: Starting from 3.0, this flag is removed and the logs RBAC is enforced by default, meaning the `logs` tab on `pod` view will not be visible without granting explicit `logs, get` permissions to the users/groups/roles requiring it.
upgradeNotes.verifyCommand: kubectl -n argocd get cm argocd-rbac-cm -o jsonpath='{.data.policy\.default}'; kubectl -n argocd get cm argocd-cm -o jsonpath='{.data.server\.rbac\.log\.enforce\.enable}'  # affected when policy.default is unset AND the flag is absent or false

upgradeNotes.title: Legacy repository config in argocd-cm is no longer read
upgradeNotes.quote: Before repositories were managed as Secrets, they were configured in the argocd-cm ConfigMap. The argocd-cm option has been deprecated for some time and is no longer available in Argo CD 3.0.
upgradeNotes.verifyCommand: kubectl -n argocd get cm argocd-cm -o json | jq '.data | keys[] | select(. == "repositories" or . == "repository.credentials" or . == "helm.repositories")'  # any output = migrate those to repository Secrets first

upgradeNotes.title: ApplicationSet nested selectors are always applied — generated Applications may disappear
upgradeNotes.quote: Starting in Argo CD 3.0, the field is ignored, and behavior is always the same as if `applyNestedSelectors` was set to `true`. In other words, nested selectors are always applied.
upgradeNotes.verifyCommand: kubectl get appsets -A -o=json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.applyNestedSelectors != true and .spec.generators[][].generators[][].generators[].selector != null) | .metadata.name'  # names printed = affected

upgradeNotes.title: Resource tracking switches from labels to annotations by default
upgradeNotes.quote: The default behavior for tracking resources has changed to use annotation-based tracking instead of label-based tracking.
upgradeNotes.verifyCommand: kubectl -n argocd get cm argocd-cm -o jsonpath='{.data.application\.resourceTrackingMethod}'; kubectl get applications -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.syncPolicy.syncOptions[]? == "ApplyOutOfSyncOnly=true") | .metadata.name'  # label/empty tracking plus these apps risks orphaned resources

upgradeNotes.title: Server-Side Apply is required — client-side apply can no longer write the ApplicationSet CRD
upgradeNotes.quote: In this version, the ApplicationSet CRD exceeds the size limit for client-side apply, meaning that the previous upgrade methods will result in `The CustomResourceDefinition "applicationsets.argoproj.io" is invalid: metadata.annotations: Too long: may not be more than 262144 bytes`
upgradeNotes.verifyCommand: kubectl get crd applicationsets.argoproj.io -o jsonpath='{.metadata.annotations.kubectl\.kubernetes\.io/last-applied-configuration}' | head -c 1  # any output = re-apply the CRDs with --server-side --force-conflicts

upgradeNotes.title: Cluster version label changes format — cluster generators can silently match nothing
upgradeNotes.quote: Application Sets with Cluster Generators, that fetch clusters based on their Kubernetes version and use `argocd.argoproj.io/auto-label-cluster-info` on the cluster secret, need to be updated to use `argocd.argoproj.io/kubernetes-version` with the `vMajor.Minor.Patch` format instead of the previous `Major.Minor` format.
upgradeNotes.verifyCommand: kubectl get appsets -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select([.. | ."argocd.argoproj.io/kubernetes-version"? // empty] | map(test("^v[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+$") | not) | any) | .metadata.name'  # names printed = selectors still use the old Major.Minor form

upgradeNotes.title: Helm 4 requires plain-HTTP OCI registries to be declared explicitly
upgradeNotes.quote: In Helm v4, the OCI implementation is more strict: if the registry doesn't speak TLS, it is required to explicitly use `--plain-http` upon `helm push`, `helm registry login` and upon `helm dependency build`.
upgradeNotes.verifyCommand: kubectl -n argocd get secret -l argocd.argoproj.io/secret-type=repository -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select((.data.url // "" | @base64d) | startswith("http://")) | select(.data.insecureOCIForceHttp == null) | .metadata.name'  # names printed = add insecureOCIForceHttp: "true"

upgradeNotes.title: GnuPG signature verification is replaced by Source Integrity
upgradeNotes.quote: Keys configured in `signatureKeys` will continue to be supported, but they cannot be used together with `sourceIntegrity`.
upgradeNotes.verifyCommand: kubectl get appprojects -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select((.spec.signatureKeys // [] | length) > 0 and .spec.sourceIntegrity != null) | .metadata.name'  # names printed = the two are configured together, which is unsupported

rules.title: Argo CD ApplicationSet CRD was applied client-side — the upgrade to 3.3 will fail
rules.recommendation: Re-apply the Argo CD CRDs with Server-Side Apply before upgrading to 3.3 or later: `kubectl apply --server-side --force-conflicts -f <crds>`. If Argo CD manages itself through an Application, add `ServerSideApply=true` to that Application's spec.syncPolicy.syncOptions. The ApplicationSet CRD is now roughly 1.4MB against a 262144-byte annotation ceiling, so client-side apply cannot write it at all — this fails the upgrade outright rather than degrading behaviour. If you set `ClientSideApplyMigration=false` as a temporary workaround for this error, remove it again after upgrading to 3.3.2 — leaving it disabled risks field-manager conflicts later. Note that only a positive signal is detectable: a Helm-managed install records its state in Secrets and sets neither marker, so the absence of this finding is not proof that Server-Side Apply was used.
rules.quote: In this version, the ApplicationSet CRD exceeds the size limit for client-side apply, meaning that the previous upgrade methods will result in `The CustomResourceDefinition "applicationsets.argoproj.io" is invalid: metadata.annotations: Too long: may not be more than 262144 bytes`

rules.title: Argo CD cluster generators select on the pre-3.4 Kubernetes version format
rules.recommendation: Update these ApplicationSets to select on the `vMajor.Minor.Patch` form (for example `v1.32.13` rather than `1.32`) before upgrading Argo CD to 3.4. This breakage is SILENT: the generator simply matches no clusters, so its Applications disappear without an error or an event. The finding is raised only for clusters whose Secret carries `argocd.argoproj.io/auto-label-cluster-info`, since Argo CD rewrites the version label only there — if you maintain that label yourself, nothing changes for you.
rules.quote: Application Sets with Cluster Generators, that fetch clusters based on their Kubernetes version and use `argocd.argoproj.io/auto-label-cluster-info` on the cluster secret, need to be updated to use `argocd.argoproj.io/kubernetes-version` with the `vMajor.Minor.Patch` format instead of the previous `Major.Minor` format.
